summary: Design-only sprint plan for branch feat/session-handoff-2026-09-12 at HEAD 056e662. Branch scope is SESSION-ROADMAP.md: PR1-PR7 local source work is merged and historical, so the remaining branch goals are outcome 4 (scoped K/evaluator agreement including the retained trace106 failure), outcome 5 (authenticated source-to-Compact, compilation, artifact binding, real SDK caller, Docker lifecycle, then admitted Preview), and outcome 6 (truthful final reconciliation). Nine sprints are proposed. Sprints 1-3 close the K track under the one-use C7/D1/G60 admission with exact depth5947/Core65536 accepted and depth5948/Core65547 rejected. Sprints 4-6 build the authenticated lowering, real executor/prover lifetime and actual Compact compilation with artifact binding. Sprints 7-8 reconcile fresh current accounting and run Docker before Preview. Sprint 9 executes the admitted Preview action and reconciles status without closing unrelated gates. Branch completion is not program acceptance: MC01-MC08, SP01-SP12, PCD, native recursion, private handoff, ACTUS and DeFi obligations remain open and separately owned.

scope.branch_completion: Close SESSION-ROADMAP remaining checkboxes and openspec/changes/language-to-ledger-lifecycle tasks 0.1-0.4, 4.1-4.5, 5.1-5.8 and 6.1-6.3, producing: fresh-audited K exec-shim source, one admitted guarded diagnostic, a repaired backend with a complete positive/negative lifecycle K corpus and independent result audit, an authenticated source/Core/profile/head/state/authority/time to Compact lowering, actual compiler artifacts bound to the reviewed source, a real SDK caller with the specified exit-retaining executor and PID 1 prover lifetime, a complete Docker lifecycle with native readback and raw exit, an independently audited admitted Preview execution with reported transaction IDs and fee-inclusive readback, and a truthful reconciliation of scoped status.
scope.remaining_program_obligations: Unchanged and not touched by this branch: MC01-MC08 acceptance, SP01-SP12 sprint gates including SP05 loan and swap Preview coverage and SP09 verification-enabled mandatory acceptance, the PCD ledger-anchored roadmap and its nine gates and five experiments, native recursion F0/F0a/F1/F2/F3 stages and RP01/RP02/RP03 gate records, private handoff and the five composition operators, all 277 ACTUS fixtures with 32 dispositions and all 72 DeFi rows, G01-G24 release gates, and the open loan raw-exit gap in preview-loan-exit-01. Completing all nine sprints closes branch scope only.

alternatives.name: A. Strict sequential roadmap order (K fully closed before any ledger work)
alternatives.tradeoffs: Simplest ownership and matches the written delivery order. But the K track is blocked on a resource admission that root does not control, so an admission stall idles the whole branch. The ledger source work needs no admission and would wait for no reason. Highest calendar risk, lowest coordination cost.

alternatives.name: B. Dependency-honest two-track sequencing (recommended)
alternatives.tradeoffs: K repair/admission/diagnostic runs as one track while authenticated lowering design, executor implementation and offline ledger tests run as a second track. One delivery implementation writer still owns shared files at a time; independent expected-results, oracle derivation, review and preparatory inventory run concurrently. Resource failures block only dependent dispatch. Costs more root sequencing attention and requires explicit file-ownership fencing between formal/k and experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial.

alternatives.name: C. Ledger-first, K deferred to the end
alternatives.tradeoffs: Reaches Docker and Preview evidence soonest and keeps the hardest external gate last. But it risks discovering a Core/K semantic discrepancy after the Compact lowering is already frozen and compiled, forcing a requalification of artifact bindings. Also weakens the stated branch order without a user decision.

recommended_approach: Adopt B. Sprints 1-3 (K track) and sprints 4-6 (ledger source track) proceed in parallel with strict file ownership: the K author owns formal/k and .moriarty-dev diagnostic files; the ledger author owns experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial and successor lowering files. Only one of the two may hold a live implementation dispatch at a time; the other track uses preparatory or review work when the writer is busy. Sprint 7 (accounting reconciliation) is the single serialization point before any resource-consuming execution: Docker in sprint 8, Preview in sprint 9. Sprint 3 must complete before sprint 8 Docker execution, because the K corpus is the semantic oracle that the compiled lifecycle is compared against; sprints 4-6 may finish first and wait at the sprint 7 gate.
